items.title: Documentary casts Ridgeway Plaza in Mississauga in a new light
items.summary: For a place that’s been around for only four years, Ridgeway Plaza in Mississauga has made a lot of headlines, both locally and abroad. Excessive noise, street racing and stunt driving, parking concerns, and sometimes fighting, along with other issues brought about by constant late-night gatherings at the huge west-end meeting place, have garnered much public attention and drawn the ire of residents in surrounding neighbourhoods. The ongoing problems eventually pitted owners of the massive plaza against both the City of Mississauga and Peel Regional Police as authorities sought ways to stamp out — or at least greatly reduce — the troubling and illegal behaviour at the Eglinton Avenue West/ Ridgeway Drive hot spot in west Erin Mills. An agreement struck earlier this year between the city and Ridgeway Plaza management, which calls for beefed-up security and other measures to address the “dangerous nuisance gatherings” and additional concerns, has seemingly put the two sides on better footing. Ridgeway Plaza (it’s actually two plazas: Erin Mills Centre and Platinum Centre) has been the subject of well over 100 public complaints since opening in 2022, prompting the city to look at options to solve the various issues. Known as a foodie destination, the plaza is home to some 115 restaurants, according to a recent city report. Mississauga officials have suggested that’s simply too many establishments in one commercial setting. As the City of Mississauga and Peel police continue to keep an eye on Ridgeway Plaza, a new short documentary film created by a group of mostly Mississauga 20- and 30-somethings shows a different side of the popular — and embattled — gathering spot (see video below). m. when the plaza “was completely packed” with people, Nicole Danesi, one of the doc’s four producers, told INSAUGA Canada in an interview.

items.title: Peel Health Inspectors Shut Down Filipino Restaurant and Bakery on Dundas Street
items.summary: According to Peel Public Health, Revrea's Grill & Bakeshop at 1057 Dundas St. W. was shut down after failing a health inspection on Wednesday, Nov. 25. The restaurant, which specializes in Filipino cuisine and baked goods, was issued a red card after inspectors alleged it did not follow good housekeeping practices and did not keep the premises free of conditions considered a health hazard. The health unit says the business may reopen once it passes a follow-up inspection. This marks the only red card on the restaurant's public inspection record, which dates back to June 2025. Peel Public Health issues red cards when an inspector finds a health risk, and the establishment stays closed until the hazard is removed.

items.title: Councillor Fonseca Weighs In as Two Townhouse Projects Advance in East Mississauga
items.summary: According to a report from Sajecki Planning, a proposed townhouse development east of Tomken Road in Mississauga would add four blocks of stacked back-to-back townhomes totalling 112 units while keeping the site's existing rental apartment building. The property is currently home to a 17-storey rental tower with 323 units, surrounded by open space and a surface parking lot. Under the proposal, one block of townhouses would run along Bloor Street and another along Riverspray Crescent, with the surface lot remaining. A second application proposes 40 stacked back-to-back townhome units at 2121 Rathburn Rd., near the Etobicoke border, also preserving an existing rental building. Both applications were submitted this month, and Ward 3 Coun. Chris Fonseca held public meetings on them last week. Fonseca told residents in September she felt the Bloor Street project was too dense.

items.title: City to Hold December Ceremony Renaming Meadowvale Bridge for Fallen Officer
items.summary: According to City of Mississauga officials, a dedication ceremony will be held in December to officially rename the Lake Wabukayne Pedestrian Bridge the Constable Dwayne Piukkala Bridge. The bridge, which crosses Winston Churchill Boulevard just north of Britannia Road West in Meadowvale, honours a Peel Regional Police officer killed while responding to a call in the area more than 40 years ago. City councillors, Peel Regional Police representatives, members of the Piukkala family and other community representatives are expected to attend. Officials said in announcing the event that the city is proud to honour the late constable by naming a bridge in his memory. Const. Dwayne Piukkala was 24 and had served three years on the force when he was killed in the line of duty in Mississauga in August 1984.

items.summary: Mississauga city hall is among the facilities closed on Friday following a water main break. A spokesperson for the City of Mississauga said the water main break occurred on Princess Royal Drive, near Duke of York Boulevard. The incident has resulted in the closure of the city hall, the Living Arts Centre, and the Hazel McCallion Central Library. “All programs scheduled at these facilities today are cancelled. Where possible, cancelled programs will be rescheduled,” the statement read. The spokesperson went on to note that a refund will be provided for any class that can’t be rescheduled. items.title: Mississauga Council Seeks Judicial Review After AGCO Approves Cannabis Shop in Meadowvale Village
items.summary: According to Mississauga Ward 11 Coun. Brad Butt, city council voted after a closed session this week to pursue a judicial review of the AGCO's decision to grant a retail cannabis licence in the historic Meadowvale Village area. Butt told residents in a letter that staff will keep gathering information through the litigation and will raise concerns with the AGCO if eligibility rules were not met or errors occurred. He said a judicial review is not a new hearing on store approval, but asks the court to examine whether the AGCO's process was reasonable. Many residents have signed a petition against the shop, arguing it compromises the neighbourhood's historic character, and members of Protect Old Meadowvale Village demonstrated outside city hall this week. Opponents say the location is too close to schools and homes and allege the AGCO failed to properly consult them.

items.title: Princess Royal Drive Pipe Break Forces Shutdown of Mississauga City Hall and Nearby Buildings
items.summary: According to the Region of Peel, a significant watermain break on Princess Royal Drive in downtown Mississauga has shut off water to City Hall, the Living Arts Centre, the central library and other nearby municipal buildings. Crews have been on site since the evening of Nov. 26 assessing the damage and carrying out repairs, the region said in a statement. To complete the repairs safely, crews must isolate the affected section of the water main. The region said running water has also been temporarily shut off for nearby properties and buildings while the work continues. No timeline was given for when water service or building access would be restored.

items.summary: , nearly seven years ago. Jamal Francique is shown in this undated handout photo. , nearly seven years ago. The inquest into Jamal Francique’s death has heard from multiple witnesses, including officers who were at the scene and Francique’s mother, who told the jury she believes anti-Black racism played a role in her son’s death. The jury heard police secretly surveilled 28-year-old Francique for days, after receiving a tip that he was trafficking drugs and had a gun. Officers did not find anything to corroborate those allegations but decided to instead arrest him on Jan. 7, 2020, for an alleged breach of his bail conditions as he left a townhouse complex. Jurors heard that Francique was shot by one of the police officers as he attempted to drive away, and that officer told the inquest that he acted out of “fight-or-flight” instinct when he saw the car accelerate toward him. Inquest counsel and most of the parties presented a total of 40 proposed recommendations to the jury on Thursday, but the jury is not required to adopt them.

items.title: One of Ontario's Biggest Supermarkets Opens on Matheson Boulevard in Mississauga
items.summary: According to insauga.com, Food World Plus has officially opened at 50 Matheson Blvd. E. near Eglinton Avenue and Hurontario Street, becoming one of the biggest supermarkets ever built in Ontario. The 176,000 square foot international mega market offers a wide selection of multicultural and specialty foods from East Asia, South Asia, Europe, the Mediterranean, the Caribbean and the Middle East. The store celebrated its grand opening on Oct. 30 and now operates daily, with longer hours on weekdays than on weekends. Departments include fresh produce, a butcher section with Certified Angus beef and halal meats, a seafood counter, a bakery, prepared foods, sushi, pizza and gelato. The outlet describes the store as a destination for shoppers seeking international foods and specialty ingredients from around the world.
